concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: The Charter Act of _______ suspended the monopoly of the East India Company over trade with India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1813**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1813:**

 
 
• This Act was a significant turning point in the East India Company's history.
 
• It marked the beginning of the end of the Company's commercial monopoly in India.
 
• The Act was passed by the British Parliament, reflecting growing concerns about the Company's power and influence.
 
• One of the key provisions of the Act was the termination of the Company's monopoly over trade with India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• This opened up the Indian market to other British merchants and traders.
 
• This allowed other British merchants to trade almost all goods within India.
 
• The Act also asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's territories in India.
 
• It provided for the promotion of education in India, although the funding allocated was limited.
 
• It allowed Christian missionaries to propagate their religion.
 
• The act allocated one lakh rupees annually for the revival and improvement of literature and the encouragement of learned Indians.
 
• The act was a result of pressure from British merchants who wanted access to the lucrative Indian market.
 
• The act reflected the growing influence of laissez-faire economic principles in Britain.
 
• It also reflected the British Parliament's increasing involvement in the affairs of India.
 
• The act led to an increase in British trade with India.
 
• The act helped to pave the way for the eventual abolition of the East India Company's rule in India.
 
• The act was renewed every 20 years, so this act was a renewal of the companies charter.
 
• The next charter act in 1833 would remove the remaining trade monopolies from the East India Trading company.
